newsitem.title: USA: Polaris sees Q2 sales, net below year-ago.
newsitem.headline: Polaris sees Q2 sales, net below year-ago.

text.p: Polaris Industries Inc said it expects second quarter sales and net income will trail the levels reported for the comparable 1996 period.
But it said it expects full-year net income will significantly exceed last year's record earnings.

"New products we're introducing later this year, including a side-by-side utility vehicle, should enable us to sustain strong revenue growth in ATVs and in 1998 we'll begin selling our Victory motorcycles, for which interest is running very high," said chief executive Hall Wendel.

The company on Thursday reported net income of $12 million, or $0.44 per share, on sales of $224.6 million for the first quarter ended March 31. In the year-ago period, the company reported net income of $13.3 million, or $0.48 per share, on sales of $278 million.
Wendel said the decline in first quarter sales and net income was "in line with the company's previously reported expectations for a slower first half in the current year."

"Late season activity helped boost snowmobile retail sales above the company's expectations, but that dealer inventories at season-end were at above normal levels for both Polaris and the industry," Wendel said.

Despite the decline in sales for the quarter, gross margins improved from 18.2 percent in the 1996 first quarter to 19.5 percent in the 1997 first quarter. "The improvement is sustainable and we expect it to continue to benefit 1997 results," he said.
Polaris makes snowmobiles, all-terrain vehicles and personal watercraft for recreational and utility use.
